title: Room for Joy to Take Root

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If a man has recently married, he must not be sent to war or have any other duty laid on him. For one year he is to be free to stay at home and bring happiness to the wife he has married. - Deut 24:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a tender and surprising law this is. A newly married man was to be excused from war and public duties for a full year, so that he could stay home and bring happiness to his wife. God built into His law a protected time for a young marriage to take root, for love to grow, and for joy to be established between husband and wife.

This reveals the goodness and generosity of God. He is not a harsh taskmaster who cares nothing for human happiness. He deliberately made room for newlyweds to enjoy one another and to build a strong foundation. God values marriage, He values joy, and He cares that couples begin their life together well.

There is a beautiful principle here, that God delights in our legitimate joys and cares about the health of our closest relationships. He is not indifferent to whether a marriage flourishes; He actively provides for it. This challenges us to value and protect our marriages and families, giving them the time and care they need rather than letting everything else crowd them out. The God who invented marriage rejoices when it is full of love and gladness. Are you giving your closest relationships the attention and care that God Himself considers so important?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you giving your closest relationships enough care?
2. How does God's care for marital joy encourage you?
3. What could you do to nurture a key relationship this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You care about joy in marriage and family. Help me protect and nurture my closest relationships as gifts from You. Amen.
